utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case IT-09-92-T, the Prosecutor versus Ratko Mladic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have -- I have French on channel 4. Could we -- yes, I think I have now English on channel 4, and I have French on channel 5. We, for a very brief moment we move into private session before we continue with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Yesterday we briefly discussed the request for an extension of time to respond to the Rule 92 ter motion for Witness RM174. The Chamber has decided on the matter, this motion, and it hereby grants the Defence request for an extension of time to respond to the 14 days from the date of the re-filed Prosecution motion with respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Suljevic. Mr. Suljevic, I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'd like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you have given at the beginning of your testimony. There seems to be a translation problem. Is the witness on the right channel?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Testing, testing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me check ... Do you now receive translation of --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then -- yes. Then I'd repeat what I said before. That is, that I remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration you've given at the beginning of your testimony. And Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning once again, Mr. Suljevic.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the following document in e-court, 65 ter 12822. We need it again. We need page 35 in B/C/S and page 10 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is, again, the incident in Petra Kocica Street, which is nowadays called Telali. Two 76-millimetre shells were found in this street. Did you have any other occasion -- was there any other occasion, actually, on which you found 76-millimetre shells?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember whether that was included in my reports. It probably was. But 76-millimetre shell and anti-armour shell of this calibre even hit the house in which I lived.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the weapon from which such a shell could be fired?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From a cannon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's look at this now. Can you see the photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the place of impact in Danila Ilica Street. Now the street is called Oprkanj, but it is one and the same incident; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the earth blown out from the crater and it was caused after the explosion.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the explosion? Yes. These are the fragments and pieces of asphalt and the curb. Probably there are also traces of earth which are visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see in this photo something has been changed as if someone was scraping the earth with some implement. Do you know how that happened?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now let us briefly look at 1D729A.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I invite you and the witness to make small pauses between question and answer, and answer and question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And may I ask, to which street did you refer? I heard different names of that specific --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There were two bombs at that instance and they landed and two streets. So one is -- the last one I mentioned was Danila Ilica. That's the old name. And the new name is Oprkanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And if I'm not mistaken on page 3, line 18, you mentioned another incident in Petra Kocica Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the same incident. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Another street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is this the -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, could you please mark on this photograph where the shell hit the ground in Danila Ilica Street, which was its name at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot find my bearings in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see where the tram tracks are, so I cannot find my bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Never mind. Let us move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And we'll return to 12822. We need page 40 in the B/C/S version and page 11 in the English version of this document. We need the English version, just for the translation of the caption below the photograph. And in the English version, this translation is under number -- three last numbers 697.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the time of the incident there were metal shutters on this window and the damage is marked on those shutters; correct? I wonder if this was marked by someone or whether this is the damage itself.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know specifically what you are asking me in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see the damage on the metal shutters, and do you know that these were metal shutters which existed at the time?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember if these were metal shutters or if there were bars. I couldn't really say that from -- after such a long time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you notice the damage though.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some traces are visible. Now what they were caused by, that is something I couldn't say now.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. We need something from the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 41 in the B/C/S version, please. And we shall keep the same page in the English version. And the text has been translated under number -- three last numbers 698.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the window opened after that, so now we can see the bars. Can you see here on this shutter that there is some damage?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean on the shutter behind the bars?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. I will suggest to that you there is no damage.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there are some white spots which are visible, but I really cannot assess on the base of this photograph what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could the centre part of that photograph be enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see the damage now, when we have zoomed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, some damage is visible. Some spots. But I couldn't say whether this was an effect at the moment when it was photographed. Because of the angle, you can see some spots of a different colour. Now whether it was caused then or whether it's a mistake made during the taking of the photo --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So you cannot really state. But in the upper left-hand corner can you see any damage on the stone, on the stone lining of the window? Because we will see the same damage in the following photograph. So it's obviously a damage in this stone lining of the window?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can we please have a look at 1D727.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This photograph is not quite clear to me. On the left, whether this is a shutter or --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Here, you can see the damage on the top edge, the stone edge, of the window, above the window.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say whether it's the same window. It's possible, but in the other photo on the left side, as far as I could see, one can see the open shutter or so it seemed to me --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. The shutter was open on the previous one. And there is no shutter here at all.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Why am I showing this photograph to you? Well, just to demonstrate that the same wall is now depicted together with the window and there is no damage on the stone wall. Is it true that when the first report was made, no damage was found on the wall itself, around the window?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I have not fully understood what you want me to say here. I do not know whether this is the same window that we saw just now with the shutter. It is true that one can see damage in the upper left corner in the stone lining around the window. But as for damage on the stone wall, as the stone is not flat, I'm not so sure whether damage could be discerned so easily.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when was this photograph taken we're looking now at. That is the window with a part of a red car, when it was it taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: On 18th of September, 2010.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And the other ones are taken immediately after the incident --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- I take it?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D727 receives number D226, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D226 is admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we would need, again, 12822; page 28 in the B/C/S version, and page 10 in the English version. The translation of the caption is under -- three last numbers are 685. In B/C/S, we -- yes. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the same incident, damage in Petra Kocica Street which is now called Telali Street. Could you explain for us why in this photograph one can see that the damage is the -- the surface damage only, whereas in the previous photograph, the same incident, the same shell, on the same surface, it seems completely different?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I move to that, let me just return just briefly to the previous damage next to the window. I cannot confirm that the damage remained from the war and that it was caused by the impact of a projectile. Because there could have been all sorts of damage during ten or more years. So I would like to distance myself from that. And as for this, it's not only surface damage and it's not the same surface. I think that it's possible that this part was with a concrete layer in front of the shops and that below that there was just asphalt and it's possible that it wasn't as thick. So one couldn't expect that the dimensions of the crater and the damage would be the same. But, in this photograph, it's not just surface damage, and I remember this as well, that the craters were quite similar.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So, in your view, this crater and the previous crater are similar. But -- all right. You even say that it's possible that the surface was harder here.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's possible. I cannot remember what it was from this point in time. But the traces that were collected on the spot and taken for analysis can be found in our report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what your report says.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please see image 44. It's page 11 in the B/C/S version, and the translation can be found under number 701 on the same page in English. We'll need page with the last three digits 438. That's the ERN number. So we need to move 33 pages forward.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Page 44 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here, you can see the fragments which you or somebody else photographed on that occasion, when the report was made. Can you please mark among these fragments the fuse.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This photograph was taken by the forensic technician at the site, and I know that because of this piece of plastic or something similar that the fragments were put in. And this was also examined by UNPROFOR members. And now I will mark the fuse. Or, rather, the remains of the deformed fuse.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You say that it's deformed. Would you agree with me that the fuse is damaged just a little and that it's almost complete?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. In your view, how much is the fuse damaged?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fuse is largely damaged. It is not visible in the photograph, but the tip of the fuse is missing. This is just the metal body. And above it is the tip which comes into contact with the surface first. There is damage on the sides as well, but not much can be seen from the photograph, when we speak about the damage. But it's quite damaged. Damaged to a large degree. We cannot even see that the fuse did what it is supposed to do. We cannot see anything in this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you examined the fragments. So we do not have to rely only on the photograph. You had these fragments at your disposal.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we talk about fragments and not just about what is visible on the photograph, the fuse was damaged to a large degree. The body was damaged. The tip is missing. The fuse did what it serves for, because the pyrotechnic elements were missing within it, so I claim with 100 per cent certainty that the fuse is the remaining fragment of a projectile which fell in this location on that particular day.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that's the fuse to be found under number 9 which bounced off and was found on the trajectory from -- on the incoming trajectory of the shell?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was marked with number 9 during the on-site investigation. It was found there. Now whether it was moved a little bit to the left or to the right, because that was a market, there were many people around. Someone may have caught it with his or her foot. That's a possibility. But it was found at the site and traces of the explosion were fresh on it. And it was included as evidence for the shell which hit in the place marked with number 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now that you've mentioned that, we have something that's been admitted as an exhibit. Where could we find that fuse today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could I first ask a question. You referred to the fuse or the piece of the fuse to be marked by number 9. What I see in the English is: "Same as previous. Number 10, mark piece of fuse." That's for a different photograph. But I wonder whether there's any confusion about piece of a fuse marked by 9 or by 10. And that is a description of another photograph, I'm aware of that, but -- before we look at it, should we first save this --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- marked photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, the photograph marked by the witnesses.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Receives number D227, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence. I'm not just -- I see on my screen number 10 marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I thank you for pointing out that issue. Actually, and we were talking, both witness and me, I think, about 65 ter number -- document number 12822 when we looked at that drawing at page 17 of B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You were talking about the drawing --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it was saved under D225.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, okay. It's clear to me now that it was a reference not to any of the pictures but to a drawing. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I'm going to ask you something about the incident on the 22nd of May, 1995, in Asikovac Street. In the vicinity of that street, there is Sarac Smailova Street; right? At that time it was known as Drvarska Street.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can answer your question only based on a city map. I can't answer from memory. If that's what we can see in a map, then that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, we can probably show you a map. But in any case, did you know that in Drvarska there was the staff of a police unit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. As I sit here today, I don't know where Drvarska Street. You say that it was close to Asikovac, but I don't know. But with the Trial Chamber's leave, I would provide a comment with regard to these military facilities. The house that I lived in - this is a small digression - anti-aircraft bullets used to come into my house through the windows. The house was hit with a 76-millimetre shell. As many shells fell there as in other parts of the city. A couple of hundred metres away from the house an air bomb fell and all the window-panes were shattered by its explosion. Shrapnel fell on the roof --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you talking about the area around Asikovac Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm talking about the house where I lived, and I don't know that there were any military targets in the vicinity. There were no commands or staffs or anything.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you don't know that there were military targets in Asikovac Street; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I didn't know that. 1

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In your statement in paragraphs 56 and 57, you talk about the Dositejeva Street and this has been redacted. This was omitted from your statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, we have now two requests on our screen. The one is to slow down. The second one is to make a short pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You did not participate in investigating the Dositejeva Street incident. There was also the Cobanija Street and the incident there happened on 16 June 1995. Can we agree that you did not participate in that either, either in the investigation or drafting the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would gladly see the reports. I did work on a case in Dositejeva Street where an air bomb fell there. I would like to have reports in front of me. I don't want to be put in a position to have to testify from memory only.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let us have your statement on the screen. We are interested in paragraph 59.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, because 56 and 57 are redacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Redacted, yes. Now we are at paragraph 59. In B/C/S version, it's page 17. In English version, it's page 9 and it goes to page 10, the next paragraph.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, Dositejeva Street is the heading above 56, 57, and 58, whereas 59 is Cobanija Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we move to Cobanija Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We move now to Cobanija Street. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What was your conclusion about Dositejeva?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is nothing about Dositejeva in the statement, just about the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Let me say that it was by mistake that you raise the matter with the witness. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I can see here what you --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just raise for the record that counsel did go into the matter that is redacted and showed the specific report to the witness two days ago. So this matter has been triggered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not any further at this moment. But I leave it your hands, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go back. Let's see the previous page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Look at the title, Dositejeva Street, 16 June 1995. This was redacted from your statement. Let's go to the following page in the B/C/S version. In paragraph 58, you say: "I have also reviewed a report made by the KDZ within the CSB of Sarajevo, dated 26 June 1995, concerning this incident. The document is done in the form which was being used at the time, and appears to be authentic to me."

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we then conclude that you did not participate in this case at all?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not participate in the drafting of the report by the KDZ within the CSB report. But if we're talking about the incident in Dositejeva, I would like to see the report because we did take part in the investigation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just to avoid any confusion that may cause on the record, the Prosecution, in its 92 ter motion indicated that we were redacting the two paragraphs because it related to a dropped incident. We kept this paragraph 58 because it related -- there are three events on this date. So paragraph 58 related to a document from one of those other events. So just to avoid any confusion that might arise, because I see we have some redactions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: With regard to this document, did you participate in its drafting? Did you participate in anything relating to that document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says that it is a report by the KDZ of the Sarajevo CSB. I did not participate in its drafting. But I don't know what case you're talking about. I don't know who worked on this case. I inspected the document. I reviewed the document --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previously. I can't tell you exactly when. I -- I'm sure that it was recorded. And that document, as a document, is authentic. It was drafted by the Sarajevo CSB. I did not concern myself with the contents of the document because I did not participate in its drafting.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I would briefly come back to the fuse that I asked you about but you didn't answer. Where could we find that fuse today? The fuse that exploded in Petra Kocica Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the material traces that were submitted for analysis accompanied by requests were analysed, were tested, a report was drafted, and they were returned to the Sarajevo CSB. They were safe-guarded there on their premises. After the war, the basement was flooded and that resulted in some problems as far as I know. I don't know whether they're still kept there. You should check that with the Sarajevo CSB.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now we're talking about Cobanija and the incident that happened on the 16th of June, 1995. Is it correct that you did not participate in the drafting of this document either?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the document. It is possible that I did not draft the report but that I reviewed the material traces. However, based on this, I can't tell you that I did not sign this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Let's go to paragraph 60. This is your statement, so I am really surprised that you don't know what you stated in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's go to paragraph 60.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, the statement deals with a lot of matters, and the witness just asks to be able to see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't have time to show him document. It's his statement. If he does not know what is in his statement, we would accept that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: The following incident is the Trg Desete Krajiske on the 18 June 1995. We'll dwell upon it for a bit longer. utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of all the streets that have changed names. But if you say so, that must be true. Some streets were even split into two parts and now bear two different names, so I would not go into that, into the name changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now see 1D761.

utterances.text: Let me jog your memory. This is the place, right, in front of the entrance number 8 in that square?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably. I was not in charge of taking photos, so I can say that you are probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would this correspond to the place where the shell landed in front of entrance number 8?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If it is part of the photo documentation, that -- it must be it. It's very hard for me to remember after such a long time where the crater was. It's practically impossible. It's even impossible for me to say which part of the town these two buildings are in without all the other constituent parts of the report. I don't know when this photo was taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you read your statement before coming here to testify?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, when was this photograph taken?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It was taken later. Later on. But the marking of the asphalt is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, when is "later on"? After five, ten --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Also in 2010.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And the marking is the same, you say. But is there evidence for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We couldn't find any pictures readable that -- visible that could be analysed so that we provide --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, so it's --

utterances.text: -- provided this one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It is your assumption that it is the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It is my knowledge that it is the same.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, you're not giving testimony here, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's your -- therefore, your assumption which you may produce evidence on. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now I would like to call up 1D764.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you do that, Mr. Lukic, I would like to find out, is this photograph part of the report that was compiled by this witness?

utterances.text: It is not.

utterances.text: Thank you so much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thus, it is my assumption that this explosion happened in front of the building in Teheranski Trg number 8. Let me give you the exact date. It was taken on the 17th September 2010. Do you see the traces of shrapnel in the asphalt in this photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the traces of shrapnel and a crater as well. The only thing that I can tell you about this photograph is this. So it's superfluous to compare this and the contemporaneous photos, and no link can be established between this photo and the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Okay. But we are working on the assumptions. Does this measure tape demonstrate the approximate direction from which the shell arrived before landing on the asphalt surface and creating this crater in it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.text: Objection. Foundation. Those facts related to this photo have not been established. Also relevance, the probative value of this photo based on what the witness has said is so extraordinarily low at this time we object to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The probative value of the testimony of this witness if based all on assumptions, Mr. Lukic, is not assisting the Chamber. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Defence has the right to conduct its own investigation and to check the testimony --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE

utterances.text: -- of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Of course, you can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But since I cannot testify and I cannot say, yes, this is the picture of that place, but we will have our experts coming here and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Fine. Fine, but this witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: If he cannot --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- on basis of his assumptions he says, "I cannot," and then to say, "I force you," although we're working on the basis of assumptions, first, establish what we are working with and then you could ask the witness further questions about it, but not at this moment on this basis. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think that the picture --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not a debate. You may proceed, Mr. ...

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This photo is not assumption, Witness. This photo shows something. Do you agree with me that the direction from which the shell landed is depicted by this tape measure?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are no traces around the crater. They are not visible enough for me to be able to estimate the exact direction from which the shell arrived. I have some doubts about the position of this measuring tape. I don't know if this is the direction. It looks wrong. It doesn't tally with how I would interpret this very unclear photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In your statement, you also mentioned what happened in Marka Oreskovica Street on the 21st of June, 1995. This can be found in paragraph 62 of your statement. Page 18 in B/C/S; page 10 in English. Again, you did not participate in compiling the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the witness's statement on the screen, please. P889. Can we zoom in on paragraph 62. You will soon see that you say: "I have reviewed a CSB Sarajevo report ..." Can we agree that you didn't work on this case, that you did not participate in the drafting of this report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we can agree that I did not participate in the drafting of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The next incident is Geteova Street. The incident happened on the 22nd of June, 1995 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, just for clarity of the record, the witness said that he was not participating in compiling this report. utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's true. We have it in the statement. I just wanted to check whether he took any part in compiling the report because it was proposed as the evidence in this trial. And we object to admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Can the witness -- I would like to ask the

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I was there. I was on the site as a member of the investigating team. The CSB in any case drafted its report, and I did not participate in the drafting of that report. After such a long time, I cannot remember whether this request came as a request to analyse the traces of the projectile and whether it arrived at the KDZ of the republican MUP where I worked, and whether some of my colleagues drafted their report upon such request, if such a request indeed [indiscernible]. This means that I did participate in the on-site investigation and in collection of traces, but I did not participate in the drafting of the CSB report in this case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move onto Geteova Street, which can be found in the following paragraph, 63, where you say that: "The report was drafted and signed by Emir Turkusic and also signed by Mirza Jamakovic." utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in drafting the document, but whether I helped my colleagues when examining certain traces, because we exchanged our experiences in all of our work. But specifically in providing the findings is something I didn't do.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The same goes for paragraph 64, incident in Vahida Maglajlic Street, on 25th of June, 1995; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My answer would be the same as the previous one. But this report was signed and drawn up by my colleague Nedim Bosnic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's time for a break, I think, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you -- you -- the "[Previous translation continues] ..." you wanted to take the break now?

utterances.text: If the parties agree on this change of scheduling, the Chamber does not oppose it. Please be seated, Mr. Suljevic. Mr. Lukic will now continue his cross-examination.

utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, we stopped at paragraph 65 in your statement.

utterances.text: All right. Thank you. We have covered Mis Irbina Street; Parmolinska Street; 30th of June, 1995. Can we also agree that you were not the author of the relevant report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean paragraph 68?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. Mr. Turkusic was the author of the report; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The following is Ilije Grbica Street, signed by Mr. Jamakovic and yourself. I mean the report. As discussed in paragraph 69 of your statement. Can we just pull it up a little bit, the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You know where the location is, Ilije Grbica 5. You have told us before that you did not know where this was.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't know where I will Ilije Grbica Street was from this point in time. There were so many streets and so many analyses, so many on-site investigations. I don't even know what part of the city it is in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Today it is it called Nize Banje Street. Does that mean anything to you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard of that street, Nize Banje, but I don't know. Only if you could show me a carte and maybe we could then find our bearings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D770, please.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The map is what needs to be shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you see a street which stretches from north to south called Nize Banje? That was the street in which the incident occurred. And the previous name of the street was Ilije Grbica.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you just tell me in which section of the map?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the middle of the upper part and the street is vertical from the north to south, and it's crossed by Dzenetica Cikme Street.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.text: Can you tell us where the location of the incident that occurred is? If you can't, it's all right.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the Svjetlost building is located?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Svjetlost had a number of buildings around the city and I'm not aware of all of them. Even if it is in this particular area, I wouldn't know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's indicated on the map below Ferhadija, that's Ferhadija Street. And Nize Banje Street ends right there where the building is on Ferhadija?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure whether Nize Banje Street really extended down to the street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes. It continues down. I'm not sure if it's like a continuation of the street but can you see how it continues that it ends at the Svjetlost building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see where the Svjetlost building is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that in this building a part of the Supreme Command of Bosnia-Herzegovina was located?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should really pause between question and answer, and answer and question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm obviously rushing too much. [Interpretation] We do not need this exhibit any longer because the witness did not recognise anything.
