utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Once again, you did not participate in the work --

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in drafting this CSB report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 71, you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please move onto the following pages in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "I have also inspected an authentic RBiH MUP KDZ report dated the 22nd of September, 1995, signed by Mirza Jamakovic and Nedim Bosnic, and I confirm it as authentic. The report sets out the analysis of my office done in order to determine the type of projectile."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see this document, 10250.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You can see what report it is. The date is the 22nd of September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please move to the next page in both versions. And can we please now focus on the last two paragraphs in the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can you see it? And can you read the last two paragraphs? Or even the third from the bottom up?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Not in their entirety. The penultimate perhaps partly but not all of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not even translated into English. Only the first two paragraphs of the finding are in -- are translated. And the opinion not at all. Have you examined this version or did you examine a different version when you confirmed the authenticity of the document? Or did you confirm the authenticity of the illegible document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I confirmed the authenticity of the document itself, not of its contents. And from this point in time, I cannot remember what sort of document I had at my disposal. It was probably possible to read it all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is the only one that we received and that is in the system.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would, once again, ask to see the witness's statement. Could we please see the statement of this witness. We need page 20 in B/C/S and page 11 in English. I apologise. The following page in both versions, please. We are interested in paragraph 72, Velesici.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you take part in drafting this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This is another document from the Security Services Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. And now something unrelated to your statement. Can a shell fall symmetrically relative to its trajectory, or is there any bending because the explosive expands and the body of the shell bursts?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A shell arrives symmetrically until the impact and then there's bursting of the body only during the impact. The position is unchanged on impact, but after the explosion, the body of the shell bursts.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the moment when it bursts, what happens with the traces on the asphalt? Are they completely symmetrical with the incoming trajectory or not? Or do they deviate, is there a deviation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not do that kind of analysis, but I think that after an explosion, the body of a shell is fragmented into a huge number of shrapnel and we cannot talk about the position of the body of the shell any longer. But, for that, I think a detailed analysis would be necessary, if you really want to go in depth into a discussion of such technical details.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not even able to enter such a discussion with you because I'm a layman in this area. But I want to ask you, when you did your analyses --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you asked whether the traces are symmetrical with the incoming trajectory or not. Symmetry is something along an axis, on one part of the axis, that it's the same as at the other part of the axis. The trajectory of a shell has a lot of axes. There's the angle of descent. There is the direction. There's a lot of axes. So, for symmetry, you need to further define symmetry on the basis of what axis. Otherwise - but if the witness would disagree, I would like to know - it seems to be a useless question, undefined question. Would you agree with that, that symmetry requires to know symmetry in relation to what axis?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Correct, Your Honour. And the question specifically had to do with the position of the projectile, the body of the projectile, as far as I understood. And it was not about the traces on the surface. If I understood the question correctly. I was only talking about the position of the projectile at the moment of the impact and whether this position changes on impact or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It was about traces on asphalt. But let's not further discuss the matter. Please proceed, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just another question. The traces on asphalt, do they reflect the exact angle at which the shell fell and hit the asphalt?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They reflect the exact direction from which the shell came. And the angle has to be calculated, and the traces are measured, and then the angle of descent is calculated. But the traces do not move.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did it happen that UNPROFOR took away shell fragments so that you could not perform your analysis?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know that. When I participated in on-site investigations, I did not see them taking away traces, at least not those that we collected. I don't know whether they did things on their own. Although I can say for a fact that they had never preceded our investigation teams. They never arrived on any of the sites before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please bear with me. I would like to call up 1D722A.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document is not in e-court, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I was informed it is. Then we'll have to work on 1D722. We'll have to rotate this image for 90 degrees clockwise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is where I left it off the other day. This is the incident in Dositejeva. I tried to pull up a different map, but I have not been able to do it for the second day. It's not in e-court, so we will work with what we have. This is Dositejeva Street, which is now known as Branislava Djurdjeva Street. Would you be able to mark the command of the 105th Motorised Brigade in Trampina Street. Did you know that it was there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that it was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you mark Dositejeva Street. Dositejeva Street number 4. And now it is called Djurdjeva.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where number 4 is. If it is the building where the incident happened --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the building which was hit by the projectile in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. Can you now mark for us the CSB, just below Mis Irbina Street. I believe it's well visible in the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, could you assist me in telling us which paragraphs of the statement deal with the ... with these incidents.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, hold on one second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber seems to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe this is a redacted portion of the statement, paragraphs 56 and 57. The Prosecution has uploaded a version of the statement with these paragraphs unredacted under 28668B, as in Boy.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now can you mark the Presidency of Bosnia and Herzegovina for us.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now can you put number 4 next to Dositejeva Street, or perhaps D4.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And can you put letters "CSB" where you encircled the CSB building for us.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know where the command of the 1st Corps was in Danijela Ozme Street?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know what building that was in.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Was the nozzle of M63 of 128 calibre found there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have to see the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 10. Just a moment while we have the photo on the screen. Let me see if something else needs to be marked. Can we keep this as the following Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 1D722 marked by the witness receives number D228, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D228 is admitted into evidence. I put on the record, Mr. Lukic, that most of the markings - not exactly the same - are found in D219. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And now I would like to call up 10153. This is a Prosecutor's 65 ter number, 10153.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see this is a report issued by your service on the 24th of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What we need in this document is page 5 in B/C/S and page 5 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Please look at the fourth paragraph in B/C/S and the eighth paragraph in English. It says here: "The metal fragment of irregular shape with the stamped mark 128-millimetre, M63 and BK, originates from the exhaust duct of a 128-millimetre Plamen M63 rocket which most probably was not part of the device that had exploded." Would you agree with me that this rocket could not be used to propel because it does not have fins and it is stabilised to high-level rotation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not analyse this. However, in our report, this is what we indicated because this is a trace that we analysed together with all the other traces collected on the spot. And this particular trace was eliminated from our analysis because it was established that it most probably did not belong to the device that had exploded on the spot at the time of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The document was signed by yourself; right? You can see your signature.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We tender this document into evidence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10153 receives number D229, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now I'm going to show you 1D747.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document is illegible, but this is the only version that we have at our disposal. It has been sent for translation. We need page 8 in the B/C/S version of the document. This is a document which originates from the Security Department of the Sarajevo-Romanija Corps. We are interested in paragraph 2, looking from the bottom of the page. It says: "The Sarajevo squadron consisting of eight pilots from the former JNA billeted in Dositejeva 2 Street, the six pilots flew on Gazela aircraft, one on ME-8 [as interpreted] and one on a Jastreb aircraft."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that one of the addresses indicated in your report was where the pilots of Bosnia-Herzegovina were billeted?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't even know that the BiH army had pilots.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We would ask for this document to be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have a number of objections to this document. The one main objection is that the vast majority of the report is illegible and blurred. I -- even through the course of not having a translation, I have not been able to decipher what most of this document is about. So we would oppose even the tendering of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise. If I could just add for the record that based on the condition of the document also, the Prosecution is quite disadvantaged at this time in being able to understand or even to be able to contextualise this document with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you read from it. That the pilots were billeted in Dositejeva Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And then your question was whether the witness knew that one of the addresses indicated in the report was where the pilots were billeted. That requires a link between a street and a house. That's not the same. Is there any --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yeah. You can see Dositejeva dva. There's number 2 as well. Dositejeva and then number 2 and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just have a look whether I see that. That is -- yes, that's not what was reported as -- yes. I see you mean the -- in the red box, first word of the semi-last Dositejeva and --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Number 2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, whether it's 2 or not, but at least there is something following before there is a dot apparently. Now, do we need the document? You have read this. We have now seen that there is "Dositejeva" and something added to that, which looks like a 2. Comes close to a 2. Whether it really is a 2 is difficult --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: It's not necessary. We can try to tender this document at the other occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that resolves the matter. I mean if -- the counsel introduced a document and is putting it in front of the Chamber, and right now I have got -- I have no idea where this document came from. I see the pages are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But I think --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: -- but I can't re- examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I suggested to Mr. Lukic to not tender it at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm not tendering it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You're not tendering it. Therefore no need to further discuss. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. [Interpretation] I would like to call up 1D748 at this moment. It is legible but it does not have a translation. It is pending. I am going to read it and you -- the document is only one half-page long.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, I'm going to object to proceeding without translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I will ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me first have a look. What is it we're looking at, to start with, before we --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We don't have it on our screens. It's the letter from President Izetbegovic to Prime Minister Silajdzic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And where does it come from?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is ERN number. We found it in the system.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You found it in the system. Most likely --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Probably the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- in view of the ERN number that it -- most likely it originates at least on the Prosecution. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: We do not have a translation for the document. I can inform the Chamber that we received it from the Presidency archives on the date of 15 October 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber does not oppose you using this document at this moment. A different matter is -- whether finally it would be admitted is a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will read the portion we want to present to this gentleman.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Suljevic, President Izetbegovic sent a letter to Dr. Silajdzic, who was prime minister at that moment. Look at the second paragraph which starts with the words: "There is another problem ..." "Chetniks opened fire on the Presidency building and they keep on saying that they do that because it houses a -- the Ministry of Defence. They know that. It doesn't really matter what Chetniks say but UNPROFOR say the same. For them, this is a military facility. Besides, the building is registered as a listed building. According to The Hague Conventions and our own laws, such buildings must not house anything that might present a military target. This is why the Ministry of Defence should be the first to move out from the building." You will agree with me that this abbreviation, MNO, does indeed stand for the Ministry of National Defence?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you know that the Presidency building also housed the Ministry of Defence? The letter was issued on the 17 of April 1995.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what was located where. This is what is written here, and it's probably correct. I'm not denying it. But, as I say, I didn't know what was housed in the Presidency building, nor which unit or brigade was located in which location.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would suggest that the document be marked for identification and that we wait until we receive the translation and then we can tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you want to tender it through this witness because the witness is not familiar with the letter, not familiar with anything in the letter, apart from that he affirms that MNO most likely stands for Ministry of National Defence. You have read to him what you wanted to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Then we don't have to tender through this witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just one second.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the last subject. My time is running out. So let me ask you this: You worked on the incident on the Zavnobih Square in Alipasino Polje; correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would like to see the report once again because that would allow me to see which particular incident that was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is 1D742. We did not plan to use this, but I just meant to ask you briefly something about it. It is an incident of the 10th of November, 1993. And you were engaged in the reconstruction of the incident. Do you remember that? You did that in 1995.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did that, specifically?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know. I would like to see some document because I cannot remember the events.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see 1D742.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You asked for it before. It is on our screen. I do not know what you further want.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: 721 ... 742. We need page 12. I'm sorry. We need page 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see report on the reconstruction of on-site investigation, 16th of November, 1995. And your name is to be found under number 5. You're listed as one of the participants.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. My name is listed under number 5, but I was not a member of the KDZ of the CSB. I do not know who Emin Turkovic is. I would have to read the entire document because this is the first time I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember this reconstruction from 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. If you don't remember ... I will try to remind you that it was a reconstruction of an incident in which many students were supposed to be killed but, in some way, it was prevented. Never mind. If you cannot remember, we'll try to clarify this with someone else. These were all the questions I had for you, and thank you for answering them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Weber, how much time you think you would need?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Approximately 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Approximately 20 minutes. Then let's ... Let's get started. If you're able to -- well, let's say, to finish by five minutes to 12.00, that would be five minutes after the time of the break and that would give you 18 minutes so that we can see whether we can conclude before the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If I may assist, I can break it up and leave some procedural stuff until after the break, potentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 28725, page 7. We ask that this page not be broadcast to the public. The materials being brought up are scans of the photocopied pictures that are part of D222, MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, with respect to the shelling on Mis Irbina Street on 27 June 1995, I'd like to return to the photos of Haris Jamakovic. On page 5817 [sic] of yesterday's transcript, it was suggested to you that Haris may have died as a result of a device that exploded in his hands. In those photos, are you able to see both of his hands?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I just have to clarify something. I think I said either in his hands or in front of him. That's what -- what I think I --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm asking him about a particular suggestion that was made to him. If counsel wants to ask for clarification --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The issue is what the suggestion was. Could you give me again the --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's on page 50 -- I'm sorry, 8517.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I believe the direct quote is -- it was suggested to him that [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... or immediate proximity. Or very close proximity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me -- and, again, it was line ... 11. One second, please. It was stated yesterday by Mr. Lukic -- he asked you whether it would be more consistent what you see with an explosion of an explosive device which was in his hands, perhaps, or in his very close vicinity. Mr. Weber now asks you whether you can see both hands of the young Jamakovic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is not possible to see that in the photographs. Or, actually, yes. Yes, both arms and hands are visible.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Let us know if you need us to zoom in. But do you see any indications of an explosive device having injured either of these hands?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not necessary to zoom in. No damage can be seen on this person's hands in these photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In the top photo, Haris appears to be lying on a stretcher. Do you know where this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know where it was taken, and it was -- yesterday was the first time that I saw this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have page 1 of these photos. It's okay for the next photo to be broadcast to the public. And if we could please have the -- zoom in on the bottom photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, in the investigative file for this incident, one of the reports indicate that there were nine vehicles that sustained damage as a result of the shelling. I'd like to draw your attention to the bottom photo here and ask you if you recognise the area depicted first.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we were looking only at this photograph, I could not say what it was. But considering the entire photo file, I remember that there were sacks or bags filled with earth which were there to secure the policeman who was performing regular security duties there. And from this point in time, I cannot remember all the details and the surroundings. Actually, I could not draw some other conclusions. That is the location which was in the courtyard between those buildings, and one entered it through a passageway leading from Mis Irbina Street. And it is implied that this was also Mis Irbina Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the car in this lower photo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you see any damage on this car?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the car, to specify examples of damage, that's something I couldn't do now. It's visible that the car is -- seems to be smeared with something or that's a matter of the quality of the photograph. But whether there are any places where the body of the car is pierced, that's something that I cannot really see. Though one can see damage on one part of the car. The rear-view mirror seems to be moved.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you able to see anything in this photo on the car that would be an indication of shrapnel hitting the car?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we could zoom in on the car a little bit. One can notice that the body of the car seems to be pierced in many places which was probably caused by shrapnel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At this time, the Prosecution tenders the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could we ask the witness to mark on this photograph where he sees the body being pierced, the body of the car.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. Let me not speculate any further, but this is noticeable.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you earlier said that the quality of the photograph was such that it was difficult. Is this just what you consider to be possible? Or do you have a more firm position as to ... as to the damage?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My position is that such damage can be caused by pieces of shrapnel from a projectile. And I was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My first question was whether you identified this as damage, whether the photograph is clear enough for you to say, Well, I see damage on this car? I'm not suggesting in either way yes or no, but you earlier expressed your difficulties in finding details in photographs which are not always very clear. So I'm asking you whether with this zoomed-in photograph you are ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am completely convinced that I what marked are instances of damage caused by shrapnel from a projectile which pierced the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And, Madam Registrar, the number would be?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could first tender the marked photo and then --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I think that is what we are doing because this is part of a report which was already MFI'd, I think, or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the D22 was MFI'd for a translation of the file. We would be tendering separately the photos that have been scanned under 28725. But before doing that, I believe we should tender the marked photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps we first do the marked one. Madam Registrar, the photo marked by the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Page 1 on document 28725 receives number P937, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: P937 is admitted into evidence. And you wanted to have the scanned photographs in the entire series as well tendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, we're now talking about the whole series.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 65 ter 28725 receives number P938, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 28724. We're just showing this document for the -- for the photo in it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, on page 8496, you confirmed that you worked on this incident and that Haris Jamakovic was killed during the shelling. On the screen before you, the Prosecution would just inquire whether you could identify whether the individual depicted in this photograph is Haris Jamakovic before the time of his death?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I just don't know whether this photograph was made immediately before the incident or perhaps taken a few years earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender this exhibit into evidence for the identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And for what evidentiary purpose exactly?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we've been talking about this boy on cross-examination for many pages and the Prosecution feels it's proper that his photo be identified and who he is be established on the record at this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There is no -- any probative value in this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What would it prove, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's just -- it's the same boy that was killed on this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If Your Honours don't feel it is relevant, I leave it to the Judges' discretion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The photograph lacks sufficient probative value to be admitted. Therefore, it's -- your request is denied.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour. Could the Prosecution please have page 2 of D209.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, you have been asked questioned about the projectile that hit the RTV building on 28 June 1995 and an imprint on the roof of the Studio C building. I'd like to direct your attention to the bottom photo on this page. Do you recognise this as the imprint on the roof of the Studio C building?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: First a basic question: Does the roof bear signs of an impact?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the roof, one can see traces, and considering both the photograph and my memory, on the roof, there were traces as if an object caught the roof surface, or grazed it, and damaged the hydro-isolation layer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you able to provide any reliable evidence as to what caused this imprint?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can suppose, if that is acceptable, that with one of its parts, the projectile just caught that part of the surface and then flew on towards the place where it fell.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 10142, page 3 of the B/C/S upload only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, I'd like to discuss with you briefly the shelling of the Dositejeva Street on 16 June 1995. I'd like to direct your attention to the top photo on this page. Do you recognise the location?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From my memory, but if this were the first time I see the photograph, I wouldn't be able to. But I do remember this, and on the basis of the damage caused to the building, I can also say yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What building are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm referring to the building on which a modified air explosive device fell and exploded. The one that is most destroyed, that was the building of the university medical centre. I'm not sure what speciality was housed there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I think that it does not -- his line of questions are not in any way related with my cross-examination. I never questioned the witness about this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution completely redacted this incident and didn't lead any evidence on it since it was a dropped exhibit. However, counsel now on cross-examination has questioned extensively about this incident. It's on the record. We do plan to re-tender the statement with those portions in it, and this witness participated in that investigation. So I'm asking him about the photos, and I will ask him about items that were recovered next.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And this is exactly which paragraphs? This is ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So this matter directly arises out of the cross because of counsel's questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the recollection of the Chamber that it was touched upon by the Defence but that not as far as the real content of it. We focussed a bit on 58 but we did not go into the details of [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe the Defence actually tendered whole documents related to this incident under 65 ter 10153.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, if you want the Chamber to look at the whole of it, then, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We do not want the Chamber to look into the whole of it. We just wanted to deal with the document [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you tendered it exclusively for the purposes of knowing what document it was that this witness said is that it is done in the form which was being used at the time. So purely for authenticity.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, that document is in evidence now. And there's -- the document contains information about this witness's work and the traces that were found. I was just establishing initially the location. I'm going to go directly to the traces, the items that were found. I believe counsel actually went substantively into a Plamen rocket that was recovered at the scene and did go into the substance of the document, and I want to the ask him about the traces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will consider the matter during the break. We take a break of 20 minutes. The witness may follow the usher. And we'll resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 20 minutes past 12.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Meanwhile, the Chamber has considered the objection, Mr. Lukic. The -- paragraphs 56 and 57 were dealt with, together with 58, not only in relation to the authenticity. It was raised in relation to the vicinity of military targets as well. And, for that reason, the Prosecution is allowed to further question the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I -- maybe it was immediately after the questions, but the question about the Presidency and whether it was the military target was also with Mis Irbina or any other incident in -- in this testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Relevant for this one as well, possibly. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In your last answer on this photograph, on page 51, you said that -- that you're referring to the building on which a modified air explosive device fell and exploded, the one that is most destroyed. I was wondering if you could please take a pen and mark the building that you're talking about.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecution tenders the marked photo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Photograph marked by the witness receives number D939.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, P -- P939, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- admitted into evidence under this last number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Could the Prosecution please have page 11. If we could please zoom in on the photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, do you recognise the items that are depicted in this photo?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are remains of rocket engines which propelled modified explosive devices.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in on the lower portion of the photo at the bottom of the cylinders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Suljevic, are you able to see the bottom of the cylinders; and are you able to tell us what is depicted here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are rocket engine tails, with stabilisers. You can see that their fins are not opened. You can see openings at the bottom for exhaust gases. You can't see much of the detail of these openings, but you can discern that those are exhaust pipes of a rocket engine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You mentioned that the fins are not opened. How would that impact - if you know - the flight of the rocket? The fact that the stabiliser fins are not opened.

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about a modified device, with several rockets combined into one. In my opinion, you cannot combine the flight of a modified explosive device with a rocket launched in a typical way. In this case, stabiliser do not have the function which they normally have in a rocket. Its -- their function is excluded, it is omitted, and rocket flies only because it is propelled by a propellant, and it flies all the way to its target propelled in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution at this time tenders 65 ter 10142 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 10142 receives number P940, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: This was page 11, you're tendering the whole of the document, which is -- let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's the photograph file related to the incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: All the photographs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nothing else. That is photo documentation only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's all photo documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, with that, the Prosecution has no further questions but we would like to address the witness's statement. The Prosecution originally tendered Mr. Suljevic's 9 February 2010 statement with portions redacted related to dropped Scheduled Incidents. This statement was admitted as P889. At this time, the Prosecution is seeking to re-tender the statement and additional associated exhibits based upon the cross-examination. Specifically, during its examination, the Defence posed questions related to the projectile that struck Dositejeva Street on 16 June 1995, initially at transcript page 8429 to 30, and then returning during today's proceedings, along with the projectiles that landed near the Bascarsija flea market on 22 December 1994. Those questions were at today's transcript, pages 8517 -- sorry. Yesterday's transcript at pages 8517 to 8522, and today's transcript from pages 3 to 12. Based on these questions, the Prosecution re-tenders the witness's statement which now includes paragraphs 43 to 47 and 56 and 57 related to these incidents. This version has been uploaded as 65 ter 28668B. The Prosecution is also re-tendering the associated exhibits. We have provided a revised list of those exhibits to the Registry, Defence, and also to the Chamber. In this revised list it includes additional associated documents with the now unredacted paragraphs, those being 65 ter 10089, 14223, 10088, and 10091. On the list, the Prosecution has placed those additional items in bold. So we're asking for the re-tendering of the statement and the admission of the associated exhibits which have not yet been marked for identification. There are 19 associated exhibits in total being tendered. The Prosecution would note, as it came up in cross-examination, that 65 ter 10250, which is item 14 on the list, had an incomplete translation, and we agree that the translation should be completed or a more legible version found and then have that tendered at that time. So, with respect to that one, number 14, if that could be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, would you like to respond immediately or would you rather --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I think I can respond immediately, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One of the concerns I have, whether we have to use the presence of the witness for that, and whether we should not first perhaps see whether there are any further questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: No further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, well --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I have one or two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You remember the incident with the sandbags and whether the car was damaged by shrapnel, yes or no. Did you go yourself to that site? Have you personally observed that scene?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I was on the site. I participated in the investigation and the analysis of the crater. I also collected traces, i.e., fragments, that resulted from the explosion of the projectile.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, we haven't seen an English version of this report, so we're a bit handicapped, but could you tell us: What I saw on the photograph with the car next to the small structure surrounded by sandbags, did we see on that photograph the point of impact at the lower part of the sandbags?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You can see where the projectile landed, as well as the soil surface that was marked on -- in the schematic as a -- a green surface. Can you see that the surface was green and all around it, there was an asphalt surface. The projectile landed in the close vicinity of the sandbags, and I believe that all that was on a soil surface. That's where the projectile exploded.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Again, we have not seen the report. Do you know of any investigation about where the children had been when they were affected by the explosion?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we arrived there, I did not see any children. According to people's statements, the children had been behind the door that we discussed yesterday, on the staircase. As far as I can remember, one boy was in the courtyard, and he had been slightly wounded by the explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was, in that report, or what you remember from the investigation, was there ever mentioned more than one explosion approximately at that same time and at the same spot?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. There was only that explosion. And immediately after that, perhaps a couple of days after that, I entered the chief's apartment, and I couldn't see that anything was happening in the apartment. And I entered the apartment in order to express my condolences to the family.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And you were then at that stairway behind the door. You have seen that place?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. During the on-site investigation, I was there as well. However, what we did most of the time was analyse the crater and the traces around it. I don't know whether a fragment was found within the crater. In any case, we collected everything that we could find on the spot at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When I asked you whether you were at the -- where the stairs were just behind the door inside, you went to that place also when you went to the family a couple of days after the incident. Is that well understood?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. You had to enter through that door in order to get to the apartment. The apartment was on the first floor, I believe. In any case, you had to go through the door. You had to climb a flight of stairs in order to enter the apartment itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions for you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Judge Fluegge has one or more questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please, one follow-up question. When you visited this site with the sandbags and the car, was the car, at that time, there in the courtyard?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After such a long time without any photos to jog my memory, I wouldn't be able to say. In all likelihood, the car was there, because the photo was taken during the on-site investigation. Without having seen that photo, I would not be able to rely on just my memory in order to remember all the details.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But today you saw photocopy of a photograph of that car, and you indicated where you assumed the impact of the shrapnels could be seen. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Several places were marked in the photo, indicating several shrapnel impacts on the car -- car's metal body.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed. I just want to know if you recall having looked at this car when you were present in this courtyard. Did you look at the car? And did you investigate if there are any signs of impact?

utterances.speaker: EKREM SULJEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, after such a long time, I really wouldn't be able to reconstruct the whole procedure. I can't tell you everything we did. I don't know whether I did it, but there were several of us who were involved in the same job. We collected traces, and we analysed places where fragments could be found. So, if not I, then maybe one of them inspected the car.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No further questions from the Bench. Have the questions of the Bench trigged any need for further questions? Apparently not. I suggest to the parties that we'll deal with the procedural matters in the absence of the witness. Then, Mr. Suljevic, I'd like to thank you very much for coming to The Hague and for giving your testimony, questions put to you by the parties and by the Bench. You have answered them. I wish you a safe trip home again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, you said you were ready to respond to the submissions made by Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the first place, we oppose introducing the evidence from the crossed-out portions, since we couldn't see which documents that were included in those portions. And, today, we went through every incident with this witness, asking him about which document he has knowledge, he has -- he participated in composing the document, and we saw that, of course, he couldn't participate and has no knowledge about the work of CSB of MUP of Sarajevo. And -- because he was not part of that organ. And he never knew what they did. And, now, trying to introduce those documents through this witness is improper. Because he does not -- does not have any knowledge and could not have any knowledge. Unless those documents were sent to him and he worked on them. And we recognised it, and we used -- we used those documents, not tendered by the Prosecution. So we used all CSB documents he worked on. But others, he has no knowledge. And I don't know about the rest, about the VRS documents whether it is still on the table, and definitely we would oppose introduction of those documents through the witness who just testified. Since we asked him also, does -- does he have any -- did he have -- have any knowledge about the documents of Army of B&H, he said no. How could he possibly have any knowledge about the documents of VRS?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, need for a brief response?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just so I can supply the Chamber with some additional information. On 11 November 2011 and 29 June 2012, the Prosecution disclosed the entire statement of the witness unredacted to the Defence. They've had it for quite a period of time. In our 92 ter motion filed in November 2012, we indicated all the non-associated exhibits that we were going to not be tendering at that time in its -- in its annex based on the redactions. We did reserve the ability should those matters arise during the examination to tender those items, which is exactly what we're doing now. So, with respect to the -- what were originally section 1 documents, the ones associated to the amalgamated statement, we believe that the witness has authenticated them, provided valuable evidence related to them. We ask that they be admitted at this time and that the unredacted version of the statement be admitted. One section is still redacted and that relates to an incident that Mr. Lukic did not go into. So, Your Honours, counsel made a strategic choice what -- what to go into and not go into in cross-examination, and now I believe that in all fairness to the Chamber that the witness's statements related to those incidents should be before it. With respect to the VRS-related documents, I wasn't making a submission at this time about them. For the record, I did provide a chart, as instructed by the Chamber, to the Defence for them to provide their comments, and we await receiving those comments back from the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I have to address one more thing. We just heard that those documents were non-associated and that the Prosecution reserved the right to use the documents. But, at the end, we can see that they reserved to -- to use shaded documents. There were no shaded documents in non-associated exhibits. We can find shaded documents only among associated exhibits. So the right to use non-associated exhibits is not reserved, as I can understand this list we received through 92 ter motion.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Maybe I'm wrong. My learned friend will correct me if I'm wrong.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would just direct counsel to footnote 4, where it said that it may be the case that cross-examination of this witness by the Mladic Defence renders it necessary to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Not only that. But if we are conferring, of course, you can continue to speak but that doesn't help very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: My apologies, also.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You refer to the fairness of the Chamber. I do not know whether we have any fairness rights but it certainly makes sense. You wanted to add anything, Mr. Weber? Is that --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I guess just simply put that the Prosecution did indicate very clearly in footnote 4 of the annex that it may be that the cross-examination of the witness by the Mladic Defence renders it necessary to tender one or more of those documents, and we indicated that it may render it necessary to tender the materials in re-direct of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That's all hereby on the record. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Only I cannot find that on the version I have. Really. The only reservation I have is concerning --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: -- associated documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I stop you there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But Mr. Weber will show to you in the next break where it is found. And if it is a version which was not provided to you, we'd like to hear from you. But let's not --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We cannot check it.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We will -- Mr. Weber and I will speak during the break, for sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's a good idea. Then the Chamber will not rush into decisions on these matters. We'll carefully consider all the submissions made. We'll then decide on the various matters raised by the Prosecution. We leave it to that at this moment. Is the Prosecution ready to call its next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. If we could just have a few moments to have Ms. D'Ascoli approach the podium. I think we can get set up in the time it takes to bring the witness in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Meanwhile, could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. No protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, Ms. D'Ascoli informs me she has a preliminary matter. I will allow her to use my microphone and I'll just sit in the back row --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but then we should wait a second. Unless it -- is it of any problem if the witness would be in, Ms. D'Ascoli?

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: No. There's no problem. It's just that it's a procedural matter. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]. My preliminary procedural matter regards the oral application to add two documents to the 65 ter exhibit list of the Prosecution. We move to add two medical documents. These are marked and uploaded with 65 ter numbers 28675 and 28676. The first one, 65 ter 28675, is a two-page death certificate for victim Osman Kapetanovic of shelling incident G2. The ERN range of this document actually shows that the document belonged to another -- another document, 65 ter 27127, already on the Prosecution 65 ter exhibit list, being in fact the death certificate, the last page of the document, which was inadvertently excluded from 65 ter 27127. As the death certificate should rightly have been part of the document that was excluded, the Prosecution makes this oral application to rectify this oversight. I don't know if we should welcome the witness in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, let's first -- good afternoon, Mr. Nakas, I presume. Before you give evidence, the Rules require that you make a solemn declaration. The text is now handed out to you. May I invite you to make that solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we start your examination, Mr. Lukic, is there any objection against adding the two documents? No, it's Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic will answer --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Any objection against adding the --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The oral application is granted. Dr. Nakas, you'll first be examined by Ms. D'Ascoli. Ms. D'Ascoli is counsel for the Prosecution. You may proceed, Ms. D'Ascoli.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Could you please state your full name for the record.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon. My name is Bakir Nakas.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And could you tell the Chamber what is your current profession.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: I am the director of a General Hospital. I've been in that position since May 1992.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, do you remember providing a statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of the ICTY in The Hague on 8 September 2010, a statement that amalgamated evidence from your previous testimony before this Tribunal but also from previous statements, with some additional observation as well as comments to the medical documents. Do you remember providing that statement?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can I ask the Court Officer to display 65 ter 28671 on the screen, which is the witness statement.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And, Dr. Nakas, once the document is on the screen, can I ask that you view the first page of the English statement, in particular, the signature at the bottom of the page, and indicate whether you recognise that signature.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, this is my full signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Can we also go to page 34 of the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And again, Dr. Nakas, I would ask you if you recognise the signature under the witness acknowledgment.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes. This is my signature, Bakir Nakas.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, do you have an opportunity to read and review your statement and the associated documents in preparation for your appearance today?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: I had an opportunity to review the entire document, as well as the associated documents.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And you also had some corrections and clarifications to your statement; right? In the meantime, can I ask the Court Officer to display, 65 ter 28711, please.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: As I was reading the statement, and as I compared the Bosnian version with the English version, I spotted some mistranslations, and I asked for some interventions to be made to some parts of the translations in order to make them clearer.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Dr. Nakas, you have in front of you the chart that was made after your observations and includes both some corrections or missing parts in the original -- well, in the B/C/S translation, given that the original is in English, as well as some other observations of -- more of a substantive comment. Do you remember this chart, and did you review its content?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes. During proofing, I reviewed this chart and to familiarize myself with the contents thereof, both in Bosnian and in English.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could we go to the second page of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, I would ask you whether you recognise the signature at the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I recognise my initials.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Nakas, there's a bit of patience required here. Ms. D'Ascoli will now read a summary of your statement. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Bakir Nakas is a doctor of medicine who worked as a general manager of the State Hospital, formerly the JNA military hospital, in Sarajevo, throughout the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, 1992 to 1995. The witness was also one of the expert advisors to the Ministry of Health of Bosnia-Herzegovina, responsible for communications regarding humanitarian aid, as well as a member of a crisis centre, which was an organisation comprised of managers of all health institutions in Sarajevo. The witness discusses the shelling and sniping directed at the State Hospital throughout the war and describes its effects upon patients and staff and how that affected the overall functioning of the hospital. The witness further gives evidence about the civilian casualties of the shelling and sniping campaign in Sarajevo and its effects on the population. In his capacity of general manager of the State Hospital, Dr. Nakas was responsible for the organisation of the hospital, including establishing medical records and documentation for the hospital. In his statement, he authenticates hospital and medical records pertaining to schedule sniping incidents F11, F12, F13, F15, F16, and scheduled shelling incidents G2, G4, G6, G7, G8, G10, G13, G15, and G18. That concludes the summary of the witness evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. If you have any further questions for the witness, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours, I do. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Dr. Nakas, first of all, I have just a quick question about the location of the State Hospital. Paragraph 12, you describe that the hospital was in the central district of Sarajevo called Marin Dvor. Could you tell us if the hospital was located on a hill or on a plain?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Marin Dvor is a plain bordering on the centre of Sarajevo. It is surrounded by the slopes of Crni Vrh and a little bit further -- further by the slopes of Trebevic. Which means that the hospital is on a plain at the very foot of Crni Vrh.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Thank you. I now want to move to the impact that the shelling and the sniping had on the State Hospital. You discuss this in several parts of your statement, for example, for the record, paragraphs 34 to 48. In paragraph 48, you speak of a deliberate targeting of vital parts of the hospital, of the intention to destroy the hospital as such. Can you explain to the Court how you developed this conclusion or whether anyone told you about such intention or whether you heard it from anyone.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Having been appointment [as interpreted] the person who was supposed to organise the work of the State Hospital in Sarajevo, I spoke to those individuals who had worked in the former military hospital. That was after the 9th of May, 1992. Some of my staff confirmed that some of our previous employees, including an orderly from the internal diseases department, Rajko Krunic, stated that they would destroy the hospital, that they would level it with the ground. As for the confirmations about the hospital being hit and what the real target was, came from a professor of architecture who surveyed the damage on the Sarajevo State Hospital and stated that the eighth floor was the heart of the stability of the central building, and if that eighth floor were to be damaged, the hospital would implode. That was Professor Hadzimusic who, unfortunately, died immediately after the war.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: And with regard to what you just said, "some of my staff confirmed that previous employees had made such statements," did you also hear any such statements during one of your official gatherings; for example, the meetings of the crisis centre organisation of which you were a part?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: As a member of the Crisis Staff, or, rather, crisis centre - we may call it like that because it is probably easier to translate into English like that. We had an opportunity to discuss on a daily basis the situation in the health service. At one of such meetings, held in 1992, we received information that our earlier colleague, a surgeon, Dragan Kalinic, who was at the time a minister in the government of Republika Srpska, said at one of the working meetings after the military hospital, in their view, had been lost for the JNA and themselves, that it would be good and necessary to target the Kosevo Hospital and other health care institutions, I suppose the military hospital included, in order to reduce the possibility of treating and providing care to the injured citizens of Sarajevo and thereby cause uncertainty in the health services in the surrounded Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Your Honours, my next questions implies calling up of an exhibit. I see it is time for a break. It might be convenient to stop at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If it would take you more than two minutes, I would agree that we take the break. But perhaps I have one additional question. Mr. Nakas, you said it was explained to you that the eighth floor was of vital importance. Did you mean to say that therefore the eighth floor was targeted specifically, in order to make the hospital implode? Is that the gist of your testimony?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the assessment of damage caused by shelling, Professor Hadzimusic and his team, together with me, made a tour of the hospital and he showed to me a damage to a pillar on the eastern side on the eighth floor. So he said, as an expert, that if that pillar was broken or sustained more damage, the hospital would practically break down and it would implode. So realising that a number of hits were directed on the eighth floor, we supposed that this was an attempt to render the hospital unfit for use.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer. We'll take a break first. Would you please follow the usher? We take a break of 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI

And it so happened that we took the entrance exam at the Faculty of Medicine together and we also were fellow students for five years together, and we also did our specialisation together at the clinical centre so that we knew each other quite well.

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Could I now have page 21 of the B/C/S and page 19 of the English. utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI

Do you see that in the B/C/S, Dr. Nakas?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it here. "Let me tell you this right now, if the military hospital falls into the hands of the enemy, I am for the destruction of the Kosevo Hospital so that the enemy has nowhere to go for medical help."

utterances.speaker: MS. D'ASCOLI
utterances.text: Yes, I take it you were reading from the original document; right?

utterances.speaker: BAKIR NAKAS
